Incidence and determinants of non-radial vascular approach for coronary angiography in heart transplant recipients.
items.abstract: Heart transplantation (HT) recipients undergo repeated coronary angiographies to screen for coronary allograft vasculopathy, which increases exposure to non-radial vascular access and potential related complications. To describe the incidence and determinants of non-radial vascular approach among HT recipients in a large HT centre. Consecutive HT recipients undergoing coronary angiography between October 2020 and March 2024 in the largest European HT centre were included, and all their previous coronary angiographies performed after HT were retrospectively reviewed. Determinants of non-radial vascular approach were assessed using multivariable logistic regression analyses, which included the individual mean number of coronary angiographies per year after HT to account for disparities in follow-up. A total of 429 patients (21.4% female, median [interquartile range] age at HT 50 [38-58] years) underwent a total of 1927 procedures, with a median number of 3 (1-7) coronary angiographies per patient performed over a median duration of 6.7 (1.3-12.9) years. The cumulative rate of non-radial vascular approach at 10 years was 35.5% (95% confidence interval: 29.9-41.1%). Independent determinants of non-radial vascular approach were HT for ischaemic heart disease (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.78, 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.69-4.54), multiple HT (aOR: 5.71, 95% CI: 1.42-23.01), female sex (aOR: 2.22, 95% CI: 1.18-4.16) and chronic dialysis after HT (aOR: 3.19, 95% CI: 1.09-9.28), but the number of procedures was not. Severe vascular complications were rare and not significantly different between vascular accesses. In this high-volume centre, non-radial vascular approach was used in approximately one third of HT recipients during their follow-up, with multiple reasons, albeit not including the overall number of procedures performed.

items.title: Anesthetic Management of Open and Endovascular Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: When, How, and Why to Use Intraoperative Transesophageal Echocardiography. A Narrative Review and Practical Framework.
items.abstract: Open surgical or endovascular thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair induces abrupt and competing hemodynamic shifts, exposing patients to significant hemodynamic instability and procedure-specific complications. Although intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) is a well-established adjunct for intraprocedural diagnostic and anatomic assessment, its role as a structured decision-making tool to support physiologic interpretation in the dynamic perioperative setting of aortic surgery remains insufficiently explored. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence and proposes a unified, stepwise, pragmatic algorithm for using TEE as a real-time intraoperative decision interface to support anesthetic management in both the open and endovascular settings. Following standardized baseline image acquisition, echocardiographic findings are subsequently interpreted dynamically (ie, linking specific patterns of ventricular loading, contractility, and flow to their clinical relevance and potential therapeutic implications). Within this framework, TEE may help translate hemodynamic data into clinical decisions by distinguishing preload depletion from contractile dysfunction, determining afterload excess or vasoplegia, and guiding fluid therapy, vasoactive modulation, bypass flow adjustment, and inotropic support. Likewise, in the setting of endovascular TAAA repair, TEE may further refine landing-zone optimization, confirm true-lumen wire positioning, and help detect endoleaks and raise suspicion of retrograde dissection. The proposed algorithm combines TEE imaging with real-time hemodynamic assessment to support intraoperative decision-making during open and endovascular TAAA repair.

items.title: Behavioral tics following sublingual allergen immunotherapy (OSIRIS): A case report.
items.abstract: We report the case of a 14-year-old boy who developed motor and vocal tics following sublingual immunotherapy with OSIRIS Acariens mix for allergic rhinitis. The tics resolved upon temporary discontinuation and reappeared upon rechallenge. To our knowledge, this is the first report of such an adverse event associated with this allergen extract. We discuss the potential link between allergic diseases, immunotherapy, and tic disorders, highlighting the need for careful monitoring of unexpected adverse events.

items.title: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation for the Management of Histiocytic Sarcoma: A Case Report and Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Histiocytic sarcoma (HS) is a rare, aggressive hematolymphoid malignancy, accounting for <1% of cases, and no standard treatment exists. Management typically includes surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy. This systematic review and case report describe the clinical features, treatments, and outcomes of adult HS, with emphasis on stem cell transplantation in refractory disease. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to September 2025. Original studies involving adults (≥18 years) with confirmed HS were included. The extracted data included demographics, presentation, disease characteristics, diagnostic criteria, immunohistochemistry, treatments, follow-up, and outcomes. Ninety-nine studies involving 185 patients were included. The median age was 55 years (range, 18-82 years). CHOP was the most frequently used chemotherapy regimen, followed by ICE; other regimens included HIPEC, DHAP, and AEVD. The median follow-up was 12 months (range, 0.5-144). Immunotherapy (eg, nivolumab and pembrolizumab) has demonstrated potential benefit in PD-L1-positive cases. Surgery (± radiotherapy) was performed in 64 patients with primarily unifocal disease, and favorable outcomes were achieved in approximately half of them. Ten patients underwent stem cell transplantation (5 allogeneic and 5 autologous), and 60% achieved remission in each group. We report a case of a 33-year-old man with refractory systemic HS who achieved durable remission (>1 year) following allogeneic haploidentical peripheral blood stem cell transplantation after failure of multiple chemotherapy regimens. HS exhibits heterogeneous and aggressive behaviors that require individualized management. Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation may be a viable option for treating refractory diseases.

items.title: [Seronegative rheumatoid arthritis combined with elbow pigmented villonodular synovitis: A case report].
items.abstract: We report a case of elbow pigmented villonodular synovitis (PVNS) combined with seronegative rheumatoid arthritis (SNRA) and review relevant literature to summarize the characteristics, treatment, and outcomes of this comorbidity. The patient was a 72-year-old female. She developed swelling and pain of the right elbow in 2002, and underwent surgical treatment. Postoperative histopathology confirmed PVNS. In 2007, she developed swelling and pain in the left elbow and underwent synovectomy, and synovectomy again yielded pathology consistent with PVNS. From 2021 onwards, she experienced recurrent bilateral knee pain and swelling. In June 2023, laboratory tests revealed markedly elevated inflammatory markers: C-reactive protein (CRP) 175.3 mg/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 116 mm/h, hemoglobin 83 g/L, and platelet count 537×10 9 /L. Rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptideantibody, anti-keratin antibody, and anti-perinuclear factor were all negative. Right knee magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed severe degenerative changes, suprapatellar bursitis with large effusion, and ligamentous injuries. Given her prior PVNS history and knee MRI findings, right knee replacement was performed; however, intraoperatively no nodular or mass-like synovial proliferation was observed. Postoperative synovial pathology demonstrated massive chronic inflammatory cell infiltration, small vessel proliferation, and fibrinoid necrosis-findings typical of rheumatoid arthritis rather than PVNS. After surgery, the left knee continued to experience recurring pain and swelling. In April 2024, she developed swelling and pain in both wrists and right ankle joints. Ultrasound examinations showed synovial proliferation in the wrists, knees, ankles, and metatarsophalangeal joints, with abundant blood flow signals and bone erosion. The patient was diagnosed as SNRA combined with PVNS. Treatment with tocilizumab 400 mg intravenously monthly plus methotrexate 10 mg weekly was initiated. After three months, CRP decreased to 0.73 mg/L, ESR to 6 mm/h. A literature review using Wanfang, CNKI, and PubMed databases with keywords "rheumatoid arthritis" and "pigmented villonodular synovitis" identified only four previously reported cases of RA combined with PVNS. Including the present case, there were 5 cases (4 females, 1 male), the median age of PVNS onset was 45 (32.5-58.0) years. The knee was the most commonly affected joint (4/5 cases), followed by the elbow. PVNS preceded RA in two cases (by 3 and 12 years), rheumatoid arthritis (RA) preceded PVNS in two cases (by 3 and 15 years), and one case had simultaneous onset. Four of the five patients were seropositive for rheunatoid factor/anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (RF/anti-CCP); only the index case was seronegative. All five patients underwent synovial resection; two (40%) experienced postoperative recurrence. In conclusion, the coexistence of PVNS and SNRA is extremely rare and poses diagnostic challenges due to overlapping clinical manifestations. Physicians should consider the possibility of RA when a patient with PVNS develops symmetric polyarthritis, and conversely, suspect concomitant PVNS when a patient with RA has persistent monoarticular symptoms uncontrolled by disease-modifying therapy. Synovial fluid analysis, MRI findings, and especially histopathological examination are crucial for differentiation. Early recognition and appropriate immunotherapy can significantly improve prognosis.

[Clinical characteristics of primary Sjögren syndrome with leukopenia].
items.abstract: To analyze the clinical characteristics of leukopenia in a large cohort of patients with primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS), to discuss its pathogenic mechanism, and to enhance clinicians ' understanding of the disease, and reduce missed diagnosis and misdiagnosis. A total of 401 inpatients and outpatients who were initially diagnosed with pSS at the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, Ninth People' s Hospital, Shanghai Jiaotong University School of Medicine, from November 2019 to March 2023 were selected for this study. The clinical data and laboratory examinations of these patients were analyzed retrospectively. Of the 401 patients, 107 (26.68%) were complicated with blood leukopenia. The reasons for the first diagnosis were analyzed. The patients with leukopenia had a lower xerostomia and xerophthalmia (39.25% vs. 54.76%, P =0.006), but a higher incidence of fatigue (26.17% vs. 12.59%, P =0.001) and thrombocytopenia (11.21% vs. 2.72%, P =0.001) than those without leukopenia. There were no significant differences in arthralgia, oral ulcer, caries, chest tightness, asthma and anemia between the two groups ( P >0.05). The laboratory test indicators were analyzed. The patients with leukopenia had a higher prevalence of anti-SSA/Ro52+ (81.31% vs. 68.35%, P =0.040), anti-SSB+ (47.66% vs. 28.57%, P vs. 51.02%, P =0.002), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) elevation (67.29% vs. 41.32%, P =0.001), and thrombocytopenia (22.43% vs. 13.27%, P =0.026) than those without leukopenia. There were no significant differences in antinuclear antibody (ANA)+, anti-SSA/Ro60+, centromere protein B(CENP-B)+, rheumatoid factor (RF)+, and anemia between the two groups ( P >0.05). The positive rate of abnormal salivary gland ultrasound in pSS with leukopenia group was higher than that in normal group ( P =0.029). There was no significant difference in salivary flow rate, dry eye test and lip gland biopsy between the two groups ( P >0.05). The incidence of pSS combined with leukopenia and autoimmune hepatitis (10.28% vs. 3.40%, P =0.006) was higher than that of the normal group, and the incidence of interstitial pneumonia (16.82% vs. 14.97%, P =0.649), renal tubule acidosis (2.80% vs. 3.06%, P =0.649) and renal tubule acidosis (2.80% vs. 3.06%, P =0.893) were no significant differences between the two groups ( P >0.05). Analysis of the effect of antibody on leukopenia showed that the proportion of leukopenia was higher in anti-SSA/Ro52+ group (30.00% vs. 18.02%, P =0.015). The percentages of leukopenia (37.78% vs. 21.05%, P vs. 16.92%, P vs. 21.03%, P =0.001) in anti-SSB+ group were significantly higher than those in anti-SSB- group. In certain patients with pSS, leukopenia manifested as the initial clinical symptom, as opposed to the typically expected dry mouth and eyes. When compared to the group with normal leukocyte levels, the group of pSS patients with leukopenia demonstrated a higher susceptibility to fatigue symptoms and exocrine gland involvement. Additionally, this leukopenia group exhibited a higher rate of antibody positivity, increased disease activity, and a greater likelihood of developing liver disease complicated by autoimmunity. These findings underscore the need for heightened clinical attention.

items.title: Incidence and Longitudinal Trajectory of de novo Hepatic Steatosis after Pancreatoduodenectomy: A Prospective Cohort Study Using Transient Elastography.
items.abstract: De novo hepatic steatosis is a recognized complication following pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD); however, its incidence and longitudinal course remain poorly defined. We prospectively evaluated the incidence, temporal trajectory, and risk factors for de novo hepatic steatosis after PD using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Consecutive patients scheduled for PD at Asan Medical Center between October 2020 and October 2023 were prospectively enrolled. Patients with baseline CAP ≥250 dB/m, preexisting diabetes mellitus, viral hepatitis, or significant alcohol consumption were excluded. De novo hepatic steatosis was defined as CAP ≥275 dB/m on follow-up VCTE. Assessments were performed at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months after surgery. The primary outcome was cumulative incidence at 12 months. Of 116 enrolled patients, 100 were eligible and 92 underwent at least one postoperative CAP measurement. The cumulative incidence of de novo hepatic steatosis at 12 months was 28.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 18.6% to 37.6%). Point prevalence peaked at 3 months (20.3%) and declined to 13.1% at 24 months. Among patients with steatosis at 12 months, 55.6% showed resolution by 24 months. Preoperative body mass index was an independent predictor of steatosis development (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.41 per 1 kg/m 2 ; 95% CI, 1.13 to 1.76; p=0.003). De novo hepatic steatosis developed in approximately one-quarter of patients after PD and showed a partially reversible course. Higher preoperative body mass index and adjuvant chemotherapy independently predicted its development, supporting systematic postoperative hepatic surveillance using VCTE.

Host restriction factors in HBV-related liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms of viral-host interplay and implications for therapy.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a leading cause of liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), imposing a substantial global health burden. The natural history of persistent HBV infection progresses from chronic inflammation to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and malignant transformation, driven in part by the stability of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) within hepatocyte nuclei. Nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs) effectively suppress viral replication but rarely lead to a functional cure, necessitating long-term therapy and carrying a residual risk of resistance. PEG-interferon-α can induce a functional cure in a minority of patients but its clinical use is limited by frequent adverse effects. Host restriction factors-cellular proteins that directly inhibit viral replication-act at multiple stages of the HBV infection cycle, including entry, cccDNA transcription, RNA stability, and virion release. HBV counters these intrinsic defenses through viral proteins such as HBx, establishing a dynamic interplay between viral and host factors that shapes infection outcome and disease progression. This review consolidates recent advances in understanding the roles of host restriction factors in HBV pathogenesis and their mechanistic links to cirrhosis and HCC. We also highlight emerging therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting these host-virus interactions to disable HBV persistence, and thereby reduce HBV-related disease burden.

items.title: Liver Transplantation for Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Survival Outcomes.
items.abstract: Palliative chemotherapy for unresectable colorectal liver metastases (uCRLM) yields poor long-term survival. Liver transplantation (LT) is an emerging curative option for highly selected patients with liver-only disease. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines. Electronic databases were searched for studies evaluating LT for uCRLM. Overall survival (OS) from comparative studies was pooled using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2 and ROBINS-I V2. Potential patient overlap between cohorts from the same transplant programs was assessed and, where present, only 1 report per cohort contributed to pooling. Seventeen studies were included, with 3 comparative studies providing data for meta-analysis. Pooled analysis favored LT over best alternative therapies (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.28-0.72; P = .0009; I² = 3%). This estimate was not robust: the TransMet randomized trial contributed 63% of the pooled weight, and its exclusion rendered the effect nonsignificant (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.30-1.35). Comparators were clinically heterogeneous, spanning chemotherapy alone, mixed best alternative therapy, and ALPPS, so the pooled hazard ratio should not be read as a single transferable estimate of transplant benefit. Narrative synthesis indicated 5-year OS rates reached 83% following strict biological selection. Post-transplant recurrence was frequent (72%-81.5%) but often amenable to curative-intent management. Referral data, available only from a conference abstract, suggest that approximately 10% of evaluated patients ultimately undergo LT. In highly selected patients with permanently unresectable, liver-confined CRLM, LT is associated with a survival advantage, although the pooled estimate rests principally on a single randomized trial and should not be generalized across the clinically distinct comparators from which it was derived. The benefit appears to be driven by identifying a ``biological elite'' through stringent selection and aggressive multidisciplinary management of recurrences. PROSPERO registration: CRD42025124542.

items.title: Brain-Specific Quantification of Somatostatin Receptor Expression: SUV max and SUVR sss as Quantitative Correlates of the Krenning Score in Meningioma.
items.abstract: Somatostatin receptor type 2 is highly expressed in meningiomas and can be quantified using [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET. The Krenning score, originally developed for [ 111 In]In-octreotide scintigraphy, remains the standard visual grading system for somatostatin receptor expression and is widely used to guide eligibility for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy. However, visual grading may not optimally translate to intracranial disease. This study evaluated the relationship between brain-specific quantitative PET parameters-SUV max and SUV ratio normalized to the superior sagittal sinus (SUVR sss )-and the Krenning score in meningioma. Methods: This single-institution retrospective study included 44 patients (70 meningiomas) who underwent clinical vertex-to-thigh [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT. Quantitative parameters (SUV max , SUVR sss , lesion size) were extracted from coregistered PET and MR images. Spearman rank correlation analysis was performed to assess associations between imaging variables and Krenning score. Differences in quantitative PET parameters across Krenning categories were evaluated using Kruskal-Wallis test and Holm-Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney U test. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis using the Youden J index identified optimal cutoffs for clinically relevant thresholds (Krenning score of Results: SUVR sss and SUV max were strongly correlated with the Krenning score (SUVR sss : Spearman ρ = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.55-0.82; SUV max : Spearman ρ = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.85; P P sss optimal thresholds were 9.00 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.96) for Krenning scores of 2 versus 3 and 29.84 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.93-1.00) for Krenning scores of 3 versus 4. SUV max optimal thresholds were 7.20 (AUC, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.84-0.99) and 30.70 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.95-1.00), respectively. Conclusion: SUVR sss and SUV max are complementary quantitative correlates of Krenning scores 2-4 in [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET-visible, MRI-measurable meningiomas. Brain-only PET evaluation may provide an alternative to liver- and spleen-based visual grading and reduce the need for whole-body imaging in selected settings. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve-derived SUV thresholds correspond to Krenning scores used for eligibility for treatment with peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, supporting further evaluation of quantitative PET parameters for theranostic decision-making for patients with meningioma.

items.title: Optimal Safety Margins and Scoring System for Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection of Crawling-Type Early Gastric Cancer.
items.abstract: Crawling-type adenocarcinoma (CTAC) is a subtype of gastric cancer characterized by lateral spreading, which makes margin assessment challenging. We aimed to evaluate the risk factors and characteristics of CTAC and provide guidance for achieving optimal resection margins during endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). This retrospective study analyzed prospectively collected data from 4,788 patients who underwent ESD for early gastric cancer between January 2012 and December 2023. The endoscopic and histopathological features of CTAC and the factors associated with lateral margin positivity (LMP) were identified. Overall, 199 patients (4.2%) were classified as having CTAC. The CTAC group had a significantly higher LMP rate than the non-CTAC group (20.6% vs 4.2%; p<0.001). Risk factors for LMP in patients with CTAC were identified using logistic regression, and a scoring system was developed: 3 points, non-greater curvature side; 1 point, lesion long axis ≥20 mm; 2 points, expected minimum safety margin <5 mm; and 1 point, expected minimum safety margin 5-10 mm. Patients were categorized into low-risk (0-1 point, 2.6% LMP rate), moderate-risk (2-4 points, 18.8% LMP rate), and high-risk (5-6 points, 48.5% LMP rate) groups. Compared to the low-risk group, the moderate-risk group had an odds ratio of 8.538 (95% confidence interval, 1.116 to 65.355; p=0.039), and the high-risk group had an odds ratio of 34.824 (95% confidence interval, 4.263 to 284.466; p=0.001) for exhibiting LMP. Lesion size, location, and safety margins influenced the risk of LMP, emphasizing the importance of optimizing safety margins during ESD for CTAC.

items.title: Mortality Risk in Steatotic Liver Disease Stratified by Cardiometabolic Risk Factors and Alcohol Consumption: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) has emerged as a new nomenclature; however, the long-term outcomes of SLD associated with its subtypes have been understudied. We aimed to investigate the all-cause and cause-specific mortality risk across SLD subtypes. Health checkup results of 2,049,641 Korean individuals were analyzed. SLD was defined as a Fatty Liver Index ≥30. Mortality risks in metabolic dysfunction-associated SLD (MASLD), metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-related liver disease (MetALD), and alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) were investigated considering cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) and alcohol consumption. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to calculate the adjusted hazard ratios (HRs). Compared with no SLD, MASLD (HR, 1.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.24 to 1.30), MetALD (HR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.36 to 1.44), and ALD (HR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.65 to 1.75) showed higher risks of all-cause mortality. All subtypes had an increased cause-specific mortality risk from liver-related disease, extrahepatic cancer, and cardiovascular disease, with liver-related mortality being the most prominent (HR, 2.57; 95% CI, 2.36 to 2.80 for MASLD; HR, 4.34; 95% CI, 3.93 to 4.78 for MetALD; HR, 6.23; 95% CI, 5.65 to 6.91 for ALD). The cumulative incidence of all-cause mortality increased as the number of CMRFs increased in all subtypes. The number of CMRFs affecting the mortality risk was the most pronounced in MASLD but the least pronounced in ALD. This study demonstrated that MASLD, MetALD, and ALD had an increased risk of all-cause and cause-specific mortality compared with no SLD. The impact of the number of CMRFs on mortality risk was most pronounced in MASLD, calling for more customized management strategies.

items.title: Long-Term Oncological Outcomes after Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection of Superficial Esophageal Cancer.
items.abstract: Long-term data on the cumulative risk of lymph node metastasis (LNM), particularly after non-curative resection, remain limited. This study aimed to analyze long-term outcomes and clarify the risk of LNM. This retrospective study included 892 patients (951 cases) who underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection for superficial esophageal cancer. Extraesophageal recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed based on pathological strata, including depth of invasion and lymphovascular invasion (LVI). In the observation group, the 5-year RFS and OS rates were 95.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 92.8% to 97.3%) and 91.4% (95% CI, 88.2% to 93.8%) for mucosal/LVI-negative, and 92.7% (95% CI, 73.7% to 98.1%) and 84.9% (95% CI, 72.9% to 91.9%) for submucosal/LVI-negative subgroups, respectively. Conversely, the submucosal/LVI-positive group showed lower 5-year RFS (51.9%; 95% CI, 16.4% to 78.8%) and OS rates (61.4%; 95% CI, 29.9% to 82.2%) (p<0.001). Additional surgery was associated with higher 5-year RFS and OS rates of 76.1% (95% CI, 59.8% to 86.4%) and 87.5% (95% CI, 71.9% to 94.7%), respectively, in the submucosal/LVI-positive subgroup. The LNM risk in mucosal cases was primarily synchronous. However, the submucosal/LVI-positive group exhibited a cumulative increase in LNM detection, with the rate increasing from 28.3% at the time of surgery to 50.0% during follow-up. Esophageal endoscopic submucosal dissection achieves excellent long-term outcomes for curative resection. Non-curative cases, particularly those with submucosal invasion and LVI, exhibit an evolving LNM risk over time. These high-risk patients may be considered for additional treatment when medically suitable, alongside meticulous, long-term oncological surveillance.
